Analysis of the four survivors of the M4 programs (all equivalent for the M4 operators; none is a test gap):
 N3-12  sorts a drone's trips by (recovery position, launch position, index) instead of (launch, recovery, index). Constraint (28) forbids overlapping trips of one drone, so in a
        feasible input (the only kind N3 accepts) the launch order and the recovery order of one drone's trips coincide: the two sort keys give the same sequence. EQUIVALENT.
 N6-07  removes the guard `if (j == trip_index) continue;`. PositionIndex::neighbours never returns the anchor's own customer and one trip serves one customer, so the guard can never
        fire; it is a defensive check. EQUIVALENT.
 CW-04 / CW-06 (offsets of the half-step coordinates of drone / truck customers by one half-step) change only the distance between a drone customer and a TRUCK customer, which N6 never
        uses (truck customers are skipped; drone-drone distances are unchanged by a common offset). They are killed by the earlier suites that use truck-drone adjacency, run with
        TDR_TESTS=test_n4_n5,test_n4_n5_oracle,test_n7_n8,test_n7_n8_oracle:
CW-04 drone customer half-step 2g (instead of 2g+1): KILLED by test_n4_n5, test_n4_n5_oracle, test_n7_n8, test_n7_n8_oracle
CW-06 truck customer half-step 2k+1: KILLED by test_n4_n5, test_n4_n5_oracle
